notes.abazina: Ma: who. Lutino ma myel, the children who dance.
notes.akuba: Goyo is to beat, also to play a drum.

guidebook.intro: Drums, songs and dances, and describing people by what they do with **ma** (who).

tips.title: Lutino ma myel
body: **Ma** after a noun means who or which: **lutino ma myel** (the children who dance), **laco ma goyo bul** (the man who plays the drum), **dano ma wero** (the people who sing).

tips.title: Instruments
body: Acholi music has the **adungu** (bow harp), the **nanga** (zither), the **rigirigi** (one-string fiddle) and many **bul** (drums), from the small **bul** **lukeme** to the big royal drums.

culture.title: Larakaraka
body: At **larakaraka**, young men play calabashes and dance to impress, and young women dance in reply. **Bwola** is the slow royal dance with big drums, and **otole** a war dance with spears and shields.
